# What's Working Around You

Posts beating their usual in your circle, what you saved, and Library outliers, one per subject.

Use when they ask what's working around them, what people in their niche post that lands, or want to pick posts to write from. Not for their own analytics (Top Performers) or live trends (Trend to Post).

**The user might say:** "Show me what's working around me this week, one post per subject, and let me pick which ones to write from in my voice."

## Steps

1. Proven posts in their circle, saves and library outliers.
   ```sh
   xholic niche now --limit 15
   ```
2. Show one post per subject and let the user pick which to write from.
3. Check what the user's Workers already wrote: ready-made drafts, free to use.
   ```sh
   xholic workers drafts
   ```
4. Get material in the user's voice (proven posts, their winners, saves, recent posts to avoid repeating).
   ```sh
   xholic context writing-kit --topic "<picked subject>"
   ```
5. For each post, find proven posts on its idea near the account's size, ranked by how far they beat their author's usual. Add 1–4 keywords so it can search live X when the library is thin.
   ```sh
   xholic inspiration search --query "<the post's idea>" --keywords "<1-4 words>"
   ```
6. Write each post yourself from one source post's shape (hook, structure, kind of ask): one idea each, the user's voice, no links, no facts that aren't in the user's data.
7. Check every draft before showing it, with the id of the post it was built from; fix what it flags.
   ```sh
   xholic drafts check --text "<post>" --source-post-ids "<source post id>"
   ```
8. Only when the user says so: save it as a draft (`xholic drafts save --text ...`) or schedule it (`xholic posts schedule --text ... --scheduled-at 2026-11-03T09:00 --timezone <their tz> --idempotency-key <unique>`). A draft is not a post.
